# google_service_usage_v2_project_consumer_policy

Consumer Policy is a set of rules that define what services or service groups
can be used for a cloud resource hierarchy. This resource manages the consumer
policy for a project as part of Hierarchical Service Activation.

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
See [Provider Versions](../guides/provider_versions.html.markdown) for more details on beta resources.

To get more information about ProjectConsumerPolicy, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/service-usage/docs/reference/rest/v2beta/consumerPolicies)
* How-to Guides
    * [Hierarchical Service Activation Overview](https://cloud.google.com/service-usage/docs/hierarchical-service-activation/overview)
    * [Manage service enablement](https://cloud.google.com/service-usage/docs/hierarchical-service-activation/manage-enablement)

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
Hierarchical Service Activation is a Preview feature.

## Example Usage - Service Usage Project Consumer Policy Basic


```hcl
resource "google_service_usage_v2_project_consumer_policy" "default" {
  provider = google-beta

  enable_rules {
    services = [
      "services/storage.googleapis.com",
      "services/compute.googleapis.com"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:



* `enable_rules` -
  (Optional)
  Enable rules define usable services and service groups.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_enable_rules).

* `force` -
  (Optional)
  If force is set to true, the policy update will proceed even if it may result
  in the deletion of resources from affected services or loss of API access for
  clients. This is required when disabling services that have been used in the
  last 30 days or were enabled in the past 3 days. Without force, such changes
  will return an error.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.



<a name="nested_enable_rules"></a>The `enable_rules` block supports:

* `services` -
  (Optional)
  The names of the services that are enabled.
  Example: `services/storage.googleapis.com`

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/consumerPolicies/default`

* `name` -
  Output only. The resource name of the policy.
  Format: `projects/{project}/consumerPolicies/default`

* `etag` -
  An opaque tag indicating the current version of the policy, used for concurrency control.

* `create_time` -
  Output only. The time the policy was created.

* `update_time` -
  Output only. The time the policy was last updated.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


ProjectConsumerPolicy can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/consumerPolicies/default`
* `{{project}}`


In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import ProjectConsumerPolicy using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/consumerPolicies/default"
  to = google_service_usage_v2_project_consumer_policy.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), ProjectConsumerPolicy can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_service_usage_v2_project_consumer_policy.default projects/{{project}}/consumerPolicies/default
$ terraform import google_service_usage_v2_project_consumer_policy.default {{project}}
```

## User Project Overrides

This resource supports [User Project Overrides](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/guides/provider_reference#user_project_override).
